solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A table on a train

parts.note: a board is a table, as in 'bed and board' or a festive board

explanation.surface: Someone describes a fold-down table found in a railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aboard a vehicle means being on it as a passenger, here a railway carriage.

clue.text: Disdain shown by prisoner over lure

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting over another means it comes first

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
to tempt is to lure or entice

explanation.surface: A convict looks down on attempts to tempt him into something.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain and contempt are synonyms for scorn felt towards something unworthy.

clue.text: Small statuette smashed on the rocks

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a Tony is the statuette awarded for Broadway theatre
something smashed is broken

explanation.surface: A tiny figurine has been shattered against some rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a business or person on the rocks has run out of money, which is what being penniless means.

clue.text: Shorten spruce

definitions.meaning: to cut back slightly, as with hair or a hedge

explanation.definitionFit: One word is both the verb to cut slightly shorter and the adjective meaning neat and tidy.

clue.text: Prince not getting up for a dance

parts.note: Charles was long the best-known prince, Prince of Wales

indicators.note: in a down clue a word getting up is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned

explanation.surface: A royal refuses to rise to his feet when invited to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' suits a down clue, where the word is read from the bottom; the surface makes it a royal refusing to stand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charleston is a lively 1920s dance named after the city in South Carolina.

clue.text: Examination of rocklike substance initially carried out

indicators.note: out tells us that letter is removed from the substance

parts.note: coral is the hard stony material built by marine polyps

indicators.note: initially picks out just the opening letter of the word carried

explanation.surface: A geologist runs a test on some stony material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives C from 'carried', and 'out' removes it from CORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, a viva, as opposed to a written paper.

clue.text: Composition from Bliss on a tape

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A piece of music by the composer Bliss is recorded on cassette.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Bliss was an English composer, which makes 'Composition' blend into the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a type of musical composition, usually for one or two instruments.

clue.text: Willing to make harsh criticism about top of league's tactics

parts.note: game means willing, as in 'I'm game'

indicators.note: about means the critical word goes around the picked letter

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of league in a down clue

explanation.surface: A pundit is keen to slam the approach of a club at the head of the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A game plan is a planned strategy, so it stands for tactics in general.

clue.text: Gas burner upset by US arsonist

parts.note: a blow is an upset or setback
in American slang a torch is a person who sets fires for hire

explanation.surface: A gas appliance has been knocked over by an American fire-raiser.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowtorch is a hand-held gas-fed burner producing a hot flame for welding or stripping paint.

clue.text: German's OK after port wine

indicators.note: after places the German word behind the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A German approves of drinking the wine after a glass of port.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Spanish region of La Rioja.

clue.text: Opposite a relation of Caesar J?

definitions.meaning: a word meaning the reverse of another
Mark Antony, written surname first like Caesar J for Julius Caesar, was Caesar's kinsman

explanation.walkthrough: Caesar J is Julius Caesar written surname-first with initial; in the same style his relative Mark Antony becomes Antony M.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of opposite meaning, as hot is to cold.

clue.text: Issue concerning tenancy agreement

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a lease is a contract letting property to a tenant

explanation.surface: A matter has come up regarding a rental contract.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue something, such as a record or statement, is to put it out publicly.

clue.text: Mother becomes furious with anger if upset

indicators.note: upset in an across clue means the word is turned the other way round

parts.note: mad means furious, very angry

explanation.surface: Mum flies into a rage when things go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Dam is the word for the mother of an animal, especially a horse.

clue.text: Pioneer in fire at bar

parts.note: a blaze is a fire
taken as written
a rail is a bar, as in a towel rail

explanation.surface: Someone at the forefront of a fire breaking out in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to blaze a trail is to be the first to do something, to pioneer it.

clue.text: Show fruit in pan to be eaten by expert

indicators.note: being eaten by something means going inside it

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: in puts the fruit inside the pan

parts.note: taken as written
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A pear in a pan is about to be consumed by a top chef.
explanation.definitionFit: Appearance and show are both outward displays, as in 'for show' or 'keep up appearances'.

clue.text: Soldiers managed to report to a dance

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers
ran means managed, as in ran a business
to tell is to report or relate

explanation.surface: Troops are ordered to present themselves for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantella is a rapid whirling Italian folk dance from southern Italy.

clue.text: A top spinning round one in courtyard

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the numeral
spinning tells us the letters of a top are churned into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A spinning top whirls about somebody in a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' turns ATOP into PATO, and 'round' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor area next to a house, much like a small courtyard.

clue.text: Friend, old singer, from a place in California

parts.note: a pal is a friend
an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice

explanation.surface: A mate and a veteran vocalist come from somewhere in California.
explanation.definitionFit: Palo Alto is a Californian city in Silicon Valley, home to Stanford University.

clue.text: About to dump mine

indicators.note: about signals that the word is turned round

parts.note: to tip is to dump rubbish, and a tip is a dump

explanation.surface: Someone is on the verge of dumping their excavation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit is a coal mine, as in a pit village or pit closures.

clue.text: Heading off, yellow bird

indicators.note: heading off means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, as does craven

explanation.surface: A yellow bird sets off on its way.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Watchful living at resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it means the letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stays alert while living at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but reads as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigilant means keeping careful watch for danger, synonymous with alert.

clue.text: Unattached clergyman, reportedly an unpredictable type

parts.note: loose means not fastened or attached

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as it sounds when said, not as spelled

parts.note: a canon is a member of a cathedral's clergy

explanation.surface: A single priest is said to be someone who behaves erratically.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a loose cannon is a person whose unpredictable behaviour may cause damage.

clue.text: Gold leaf in centre of blue room, out of place

indicators.note: out of place means the letters are rearranged
centre of picks the two middle letters of the colour word

explanation.surface: Gilding sits in the middle of a blue room where it does not belong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' gives LU from 'blue'; 'out of place' mixes LU with ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormolu is gilded bronze or brass, or the gold-coloured leaf used for decorative gilding.

clue.text: Film girl's short engagement

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Gigi is the title heroine of the 1958 musical film

explanation.surface: A movie actress gets a brief booking.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a single booked performance, an engagement for a musician.

clue.text: Look for a town in Newfoundland

definitions.meaning: a town in Canada known for its airport, a transatlantic refuelling stop

explanation.definitionFit: Gander is slang for a quick look and also the name of a Newfoundland town.

clue.text: Country song about soldiers

indicators.note: about means the song goes around the soldiers

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
men are soldiers, as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A national ballad concerns the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a nation in the South Caucasus, bordering Turkey and Georgia.

clue.text: Average Agatha Christie novel?

definitions.meaning: the 1941 Tommy and Tuppence spy story titled ...?

explanation.definitionFit: Norm means a standard or average, and N or M? is a Christie thriller title run together.

clue.text: Troublemaker in Russian government with new leader

indicators.note: a new leader means the first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: the Kremlin is the seat of Russian government, used to mean the government itself

explanation.surface: Someone stirring up trouble inside Moscow's administration under a fresh boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The new first letter G is not separately clued; changing K to G is the only swap giving a word for troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary mischievous sprite blamed for mechanical faults, hence a source of trouble.

clue.text: Happy, former PM having lost weight

indicators.note: having lost means that part is removed

parts.note: William Gladstone was a 19th-century British prime minister
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: An ex-premier is pleased to have slimmed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad is a synonym for happy or pleased.

clue.text: Roof worker, 50, entering bank

indicators.note: entering puts the numeral inside the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row or bank, as of seats
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old roofer goes into a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiler lays tiles, typically on roofs, so he works on a roof.

clue.text: Duff gen on vestibule in church presents a difficulty

indicators.note: on in an across clue means coming after
in puts the vestibule word inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a hall is an entrance vestibule

indicators.note: duff means faulty or useless, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Faulty information about a church porch causes problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duff' looks like a verb but is British slang for faulty, signalling rearrangement; 'gen' is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A challenge is a demanding task that tests ability, so it is a difficulty to overcome.
